subject: Trading
title: Options on Indexes vs. Stocks
description: A 60-second lesson on Options on Indexes vs. Stocks.

hook.text: SPX options settle in cash. Stock options deliver shares. This difference changes everything about how they're traded.

buildup.text: Index options (SPX, NDX) are European-style and cash-settled. Stock options (AAPL, TSLA) are American-style.

discovery.text: Cash settlement means no shares change hands—just the profit or loss amount. Simpler for big portfolio hedges.

twist.text: SPX options have tax advantages in the U.S.: 60% of gains are taxed as long-term, regardless of holding period.

climax.text: Institutions overwhelmingly trade index options for hedging. Retail traders favor stock options for speculation.

punchline.text: Different settlement, different uses, different taxes.

quiz.question: What does cash settlement mean for index options?
options: You must pay in cash upfront
No shares change hands—only the profit or loss is settled
They trade only during cash hours
